rows: Cour Saint-Guillaume
Charles Marville photographed this quiet courtyard in Paris in the 1860s, when much of old Paris was being torn down. His careful pictures kept a record of places that were about to vanish.
Why would a city photographer record places that were going to be torn down?
Nadar and His Wife Ernestine in a Balloon
Nadar loved balloons and took the first aerial photographs of Paris from one in 1858. Here he poses with his wife Ernestine in the basket of a balloon around 1865.
What would it feel like to float in a basket?
Rue de Constantine, Paris

Charles Marville photographed this street on the Île de la Cité, an area of old crooked lanes that was rebuilt in the 1860s. His pictures have no crowds, because the cameras were so slow that moving people disappeared.
Where did the people go?
Crowd at Lincoln's Second Inauguration
A huge crowd gathered at the U.S. Capitol on March 4, 1865, to watch Abraham Lincoln take the oath for his second term. The Civil War was almost over, and Lincoln spoke of 'malice toward none.'
Why do you think so many people came?
Ruins of the Richmond and Petersburg Railroad Bridge
Alexander Gardner photographed the burned railroad bridge in Richmond, Virginia, in April 1865. Retreating Confederates set it on fire as they left the capital.
Why did they burn the bridge?
The Ruins of Richmond
Andrew J. Russell photographed the burned heart of Richmond, Virginia, in April 1865. Rows of empty brick walls stand where shops and warehouses had been.
What parts of a building can survive a fire?
The Mills House, Charleston
George Barnard photographed a hotel in Charleston, South Carolina, standing next to the ruins of burned buildings in 1865. The Mills House survived while its neighbors were burned.
What would it be like to stay in a hotel with ruins next door?
Ruins of a Tobacco Warehouse, Richmond
In April 1865 Richmond, Virginia, burned as Confederates left. This tobacco warehouse is a shell of brick walls and open windows.
Why were tobacco warehouses important in Richmond?
Ruins of Secession Hall, Charleston
George Barnard photographed the shell of the hall in Charleston where South Carolina voted to leave the Union in 1860. The building burned in 1861 and stood in ruins.
Why would a photographer visit this ruin?
Savannah, Georgia: Ruins of Houses
Samuel Cooley photographed the ruined houses of Savannah, Georgia, at the end of the Civil War. The city was spared when General Sherman took it in December 1864, but nearby places were damaged.
What would you do if your house had been wrecked?
Ruins of a Woolen Mill, Petersburg
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed a burned woolen mill in Petersburg, Virginia, in 1865. Mills made cloth for uniforms, so armies burned them.
Why would an army burn a cloth mill?
Ruins of the Gallego Mills, Richmond
The Gallego Mills in Richmond were among the biggest flour mills in the world before the Civil War. They were burned in April 1865, and the shell of the mill stood by the river.
Why was a flour mill so important in a war?
Ruins of Mayo's Bridge, Richmond
Mayo's Bridge crossed the James River in Richmond, Virginia. It was burned in April 1865, and the stone piers and burned timbers stayed in the river.
Why would a bridge in a capital city matter?
Ruins of the State Arsenal, Richmond
The Virginia state arsenal in Richmond stored guns and ammunition. It burned in April 1865, and the walls are scorched.
What would you find in an arsenal?
Laying the Cornerstone of the Soldiers' Monument, Gettysburg
On July 4, 1865, people gathered at Gettysburg to lay the cornerstone of a monument to Union soldiers. It was the first anniversary after the battle, and Gardner photographed the ceremony.
Why do people build monuments to soldiers?
Woman in Lorraine Dress

Adolphe Braun photographed a woman in the traditional costume of Lorraine, a region of France. After the Franco-Prussian War, Prussia seized much of the region, and traditional dress became a symbol of French identity.
Why would clothing become a symbol?
Hong Kong Harbour View
William Pryor Floyd was a former sailor who became a photographer in Hong Kong around 1865. His views show a young British colony on the coast of China, with ships crowding the harbor.
How many ships can you count?
Hong Kong Street View
Floyd's pictures of Hong Kong are praised for their clear organization and elegance. This one shows a town growing quickly because of the busy sea trade.
What does the picture show about trade?
Chinese Landscape
Lai Fong, a Chinese photographer in Hong Kong, made landscapes for travelers. Most of his customers were Western visitors who wanted souvenirs of China.
What would a visitor want to remember?
Young Alsatian Woman
Adolphe Braun photographed a young woman in the dress of Alsace, a region on the French-German border. He was a textile designer who became a leading photographer.
What do the clothes tell you about where she is from?
Syrian Muslim Women in Beirut, City Costume
Félix Bonfils settled in Beirut with his family and photographed local people in the clothes of the city. Visitors bought these pictures as souvenirs of the Middle East.
How could a photograph be a souvenir?
Great Dismal Swamp, Virginia
Israel Cook Russell photographed the Great Dismal Swamp, a huge wetland on the border of Virginia and North Carolina. Escaped slaves had hidden in its thick forest.
Why would it be a good hiding place?
Have We Not Heard the Bridegroom Is So Sweet
Julia Margaret Cameron staged this photograph from a line of poetry in 1868. She used neighbors and relatives as models, dressed them in costume and let the focus go soft.
What mood does the soft focus give the picture?
Mono Lake, Volcano
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed a volcanic cone at Mono Lake in California in 1868, working for a survey of the American West. He is famous for his strange, empty landscapes.
What would you feel standing in such an empty place?
Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed the American poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow in 1868 during his visit to England. His white beard and long hair made him look like a wise old man.
What do you think a poet's face looks like?
Joseph Joachim
Joseph Joachim was a Hungarian violinist, one of the greatest of the 1800s. Cameron photographed him in 1868, with the dramatic light and close view she was famous for.
What instrument do you play or want to play?
Elaine
Cameron photographed this young woman as Elaine, a character in Tennyson's poems about King Arthur. She illustrated the Idylls of the King with her photographs.
Which story would you act out for a photograph?
The Parinirvana of Buddha, Gal Vihara, Polonnaruwa
Joseph Lawton photographed a giant stone Buddha lying down at Polonnaruwa in Sri Lanka. It was carved from a granite cliff about 900 years ago and is 14 meters long.
How do you think the sculptors carved something so large?
Man with Walking Stick
Auguste Giraudon was a Parisian publisher of photographs who hired artists to pose models as peasants and workers. This man with his walking stick was posed for a series of country types.
Why would a publisher use models for a picture of peasants?
Two Shepherdesses Resting with Two Sheep
This staged picture shows two shepherdesses with their sheep. Giraudon sold photographs like this to painters, who used them as models for pictures.
Why would a painter use a photograph as a model?
Jewish Woman in Algeria
Jean Geiser photographed a woman in Algeria in about 1870. Photographers sold such pictures as studies of costume, though a person's own story was often left out.
What would you ask her if you could?
Maharaja Ranbir Singh and Court
Bourne and Shepherd photographed Ranbir Singh, ruler of Jammu and Kashmir, with his sons and court. Their studios took pictures of kings and officials across India.
How can you tell who the ruler is?
Whitney Glacier and Mount Shasta

Carleton Watkins photographed the Whitney Glacier and Mount Shasta in California in 1870, from the summit of the smaller peak Shastina. Watkins hauled his huge camera and glass plates up the mountain.
Why do you think the glacier is so important to scientists?
Combe Martin Bay
Francis Frith photographed the cove at Combe Martin on the coast of Devon, England. His pictures were sold in shops across England.
What would you do on this beach?
Balaustion
Julia Margaret Cameron photographed this woman as Balaustion, a Greek heroine in a poem by Robert Browning. She dressed models in costume and let them look away.
What do you imagine the heroine is looking at?
The Bath, a Dripping Spring in Kanab Canyon
William H. Bell photographed a spring dripping from a canyon wall in Arizona in 1872, with a temperature of 69 degrees. The expedition he joined was exploring the Colorado River.
Why would explorers note the temperature of a spring?
Canyon of Kanab Wash, Looking South
Bell was the staff photographer for the 1872 survey of the Colorado River led by John Wesley Powell's team. He photographed the canyon walls rising high on each side.
How tall do the canyon walls look?
Disgust
Oscar Rejlander made photographs for Charles Darwin's 1872 book The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals. This picture was meant to show disgust on a person's face.
What is your face like when you taste something yucky?
Navajo Life near Old Fort Defiance
Timothy O'Sullivan photographed Navajo people near Fort Defiance in New Mexico Territory in 1873, after the 1868 treaty let them return to their homeland. The picture shows hogans and daily life.
What can you tell about daily life from the picture?
The Island Pagoda
John Thomson photographed a pagoda on an island in the Min River in China. He set up a studio in Hong Kong in 1868 and traveled widely across China, photographing places that few Europeans had seen.
Why might a pagoda be on an island?
Yuen Fu Rapids
Thomson photographed the rapids on the North River in China as boatmen guided a boat. Boat travel was the main way to move around, and the rapids were dangerous.
How would you steer a boat through rapids?
Yuen Fu Monastery
Thomson photographed a monastery in southern China on his journey up the North River. His books of photographs helped Europeans see inland China.
What do the roofs and trees look like?
Sarah Bernhardt as Zaïre
Étienne Carjat photographed the actress Sarah Bernhardt in 1874 as the heroine of Voltaire's play Zaïre. She was already France's most celebrated actress.
How would you pose to look like a tragic heroine?
Good Morning
Joshua Smith photographed a staged scene, called Good Morning, in the 1870s. Posed scenes were popular and meant to amuse viewers.
Who do you think is saying good morning?
Émile Angier
Antoine Samuel Adam-Salomon, a sculptor turned photographer, photographed Émile Angier with dramatic lighting. His portraits looked like carved busts with strong light on one side.
Which side of the face is lit?
Dufaure
Jules Armand Dufaure was a French statesman who served as prime minister several times. Adam-Salomon photographed him in the 1870s with sculptural light.
How does the light make the face look carved?
Grindelwald, Upper Glacier
Adolphe Braun photographed the Upper Grindelwald Glacier in the Swiss Alps. Climbing up with big cameras and glass plates was a feat, and his Alpine pictures were popular souvenirs.
What shapes do the ice and rock make?
Buddhist Temple, Kalani
This photograph shows a sacred Buddhist site near Colombo in Sri Lanka, perhaps a sacred fig tree planted from a branch of the tree under which Buddha sat. Pilgrims have visited for centuries.
Why would a tree be sacred?
A Commercial Street in Guangzhou
Lai Fong photographed a busy shopping street in Guangzhou, then called Canton, a port city on the Pearl River. The narrow street is crowded with signs, shops and people.
What kinds of shops do you see?
A Convict's Home
John Thomson and Adolphe Smith photographed poor families in London for a book called Street Life in London (1877). A convict's home shows the hard life of families left behind.
Why would someone make a book about poor people?
Street Advertising

Two men paste a large poster on a wall in London in the late 1870s. Thomson photographed the street trades of London for Street Life in London, and this picture shows how advertising worked before radio and television.
How do advertisers reach people today?
Covent Garden Flower Women
Thomson photographed women who sold flowers outside Covent Garden market in London. The flower women were a familiar sight and worked in all weather.
What flowers might they be selling?
Recruiting Sergeants at Westminster
Recruiting sergeants stood near Westminster Bridge in London to sign up young men for the army. Thomson photographed them in the 1870s for Street Life in London.
How do armies find new soldiers today?
Sufferers from the Floods
Thomson and Adolphe Smith photographed a family whose home was flooded. They wanted readers to see how floods hurt the poor.
How would you help a family hit by a flood?
Council of Regency, Gwalior

Raja Deen Dayal photographed the council that ruled Gwalior while its young ruler grew up. Deen Dayal became one of the greatest Indian photographers, and the Nizam of Hyderabad later appointed him court photographer.
Why would a young ruler need a council?
Captain Harris and Ruston, Jhansi
Raja Deen Dayal photographed British officers at Jhansi in India in 1877 for an album. He was the first Indian photographer to become famous across India.
What do the officers wear?
Judging at the Horse Show at Jhansi
Deen Dayal photographed a horse show at Jhansi in India. Horse shows were a favorite way for British and Indian officials to meet.
What would the judges look for in a horse?
The Amir Sher Ali's Son
John Burke photographed people involved in the Second Anglo-Afghan War, which began in 1878. He traveled with the army and made one of the first photographic records of Afghanistan.
Why would a photographer travel with an army?
Amir Yakub Khan and His Officials
John Burke photographed the Afghan ruler Yakub Khan with his advisers. Photographs like this show how leaders posed during a war.
What can you tell about the men from their clothes?
Group of Afridis
John Burke photographed a group of Afridi tribesmen, who live in the mountains between Afghanistan and Pakistan. They were famous fighters.
What do you notice about the weapons and clothes?
Lalpura from the Ferry
Burke photographed the village of Lalpura from a ferry on the Kabul River. His pictures show the landscape through which the army traveled.
What would it be like to cross a river on a ferry?
View from the Top of the Rock, Trichinopoly
Nicholas and Company photographed the city of Trichinopoly, now Tiruchirappalli, in India, from the top of the great rock. Below you can see the town and the Ranganathaswamy Temple.
How many temple towers can you spot?
Cinnabar Mountain, Devil's Slide
Frank Jay Haynes photographed Devil's Slide, a stripe of red rock on a mountain near Yellowstone National Park, in 1880. Haynes later became the official photographer of Yellowstone.
What makes the red stripe look so strange?
Ceylonese Woman
European photographers in the colonies often made portraits of the local people, and they sold them to visitors. This woman from Ceylon, now Sri Lanka, stands in the dress of her village.
How could a photograph hide a person's own story?
Sinhalese Man
A Sinhalese man wears a Western jacket and shirt, but he keeps his traditional hairstyle. His clothes show how two cultures mixed in Ceylon in the 1800s.
Which parts of his clothes come from which culture?
Veddahs of Ceylon
The Veddahs are an indigenous people of Sri Lanka, who for centuries lived by hunting and gathering in the forests. Photographers in the 1880s visited them as a curiosity.
Why do you think they were famous with visitors?
Group at Nortekande Bungalow
British officials and their families relaxed at a bungalow on a leisurely afternoon in India. Photographs like this show how colonial life looked to those who lived it.
What would you do on a leisurely afternoon without screens?
A Stiff Pull
Peter Henry Emerson photographed boatmen pulling hard on a boat on the Norfolk Broads in England. He wanted photographs that looked natural, and he disliked fakes.
What do you think a stiff pull feels like?
Hong Lim Green, Singapore

The London Stereoscopic Company photographed Hong Lim Green, an open space in the Chinese district of Singapore, in 1882. The Chinese were the biggest ethnic group in Singapore, which was a busy port.
What do you think the open space was used for?
Narmada River at Omkareshwar
Raja Deen Dayal made a two-part panorama of the Narmada River at the temple island of Omkareshwar in India. He placed the river in front of the camera and joined two plates for a wide view.
How does joining two pictures make a wide view?
Edwin Booth's Boat House, Newport
Louise Deshong Woodbridge, a Philadelphia socialite, photographed the boat house of the famous actor Edwin Booth in Newport, Rhode Island, on August 6, 1884. She was an amateur with a good eye.
Why would a rich actor have a boat house?
Elephant Walking
Eadweard Muybridge photographed an elephant walking, with cameras set to snap one after another. His series of animals in motion in the 1880s helped people see how bodies move.
How does the elephant move its legs?
Hell's Half Acre, Prismatic Springs

Frank Jay Haynes photographed a steaming hot spring at Yellowstone National Park in 1885. The colors in the pool come from heat-loving microbes, but black-and-white pictures could only show the steam and shapes.
What would the colors be like in real life?
Crowell Children at Avondale
Thomas Eakins, the American painter, photographed children outside in the 1880s. He used photography to study how bodies and light look, as a help for his paintings.
How is a photograph useful for a painter?
Aurangzeb's Mosque, Benares
A Swiss firm printed this view of the mosque of Aurangzeb, the sixth Mughal emperor, in Benares, now Varanasi. The mosque stands high above the Ganges, with tall minarets.
What do you notice about the mosque's towers?
Clara L. White as a Child
This small portrait of a girl named Clara L. White is a photograph painted by hand with colors. The painter's skill gives it an intimate and glowing look.
Why would someone paint over a photograph?
Mahmud Gawan Madrasa, Bidar
Raja Deen Dayal photographed the ruined college of Mahmud Gawan in Bidar, India, built in the 1400s. The tower's pattern echoes designs on Bidri metalwork.
What patterns do you see on the tower?
Dedication of the Washington Monument
The Washington Monument in Washington, D.C., was dedicated on February 21, 1885. A huge crowd gathered at its base, and at 555 feet it was the tallest structure in the world for a while.
What do you think the day was like?
His Highness the Maharaja of Rewa
Raja Deen Dayal photographed the Maharaja of Rewa in 1886. Being an Indian photographer may have helped him get access to rulers and their courts.
Why might a ruler trust a local photographer?
Coming Home from the Marshes
Peter Henry Emerson photographed marsh workers carrying reeds home on the Norfolk Broads. He printed on platinum paper for a soft tone, and he wanted photography to be treated as a true art.
What do you think the workers carry?
Alfred Stieglitz Self-Portrait
Alfred Stieglitz photographed himself in Freienwalde, Germany, in 1886 when he was a young student. He later became the great champion of photography as art in America.
Why would a student photograph himself?
Mrs. and Miss Lyall, Shimla
Raja Deen Dayal photographed Mrs. and Miss Lyall in Shimla, India, in 1887. Many of his Shimla portraits include rickshaws, which were the way to get around the hill town.
How is a rickshaw different from a car?
A Fisherman at Home
Peter Henry Emerson published this photograph in his 1887 book Pictures from Life in Field and Fen. It shows a fisherman in his home in the English fens.
What does a fisherman's home look like?
At Plough, the End of the Furrow
A farmer turns his plough and horses at the end of the field in Emerson's 1887 book. Emerson photographed rural life in England as it was disappearing.
How would you plough a field with horses?
A Winter's Morning
Peter Henry Emerson photographed a cold winter's morning in the English fens in 1887. The soft light and mist are typical of his natural style.
What do you hear on a quiet winter morning?
A Dame's School
Emerson photographed a dame school, a small village school run by an old woman, in his 1887 book. Children learned reading and writing in the dame's own kitchen.
What would a school in a kitchen be like?
The Last Joke, Bellagio
Alfred Stieglitz photographed two Italian men laughing together in the street in Bellagio, in 1887. It shows his early love of everyday life and won a prize in a photography contest.
What might the joke be?
Snowscape, Berlin
Alfred Stieglitz photographed a snowy street in Berlin in 1888 while he was a student in Germany. He loved difficult conditions such as snow and rain.
How does snow change a city?
